HUD notes the Commission's recommendation that the Cambridge Historical Commission be consulted to review and suggest appropriate historic treatments regarding the use of materials to highlight historic development. HUD will advise the CRA that the Authority's design advisory group seriously consider this recommendation. HUD notes also that the Commission believes that the effort to relate visually the new development to its surroundings will lead to a design concept "reflective of continuing urban revitalization and sensitive to the urban qualities which define Kendall Square.
Executive Office of Environmental (Affairs (August 9, 1977)
Noise Impact:
Regarding EOEA's statement that the final report should include established critical noise standards for both land use development and construction activities, it should be noted that such standards are presently incorporated in Cambridge City Ordinance No. 877 (Section 13-10 of the Code of City of Cambridge), entitled Regulations for the Control of Noise. Construction contractors and land developers and users will be required, of course, to comply with this ordinance.
Regarding the establishment of truck routes and time restrictions, the Authority is actively working with the Cambridge Community Development Department in the preparation of engineering and environmental studies in connection with proposed roadway improvements and connections in the East Cambridge neighborhood. The proposed improvements are concerned with establishing traffic circulation areas. The routes will interrelate with the traffic circulation plan for the Kendall Square Area. In addition, Cambridge is considering the adoption of ordinances which will prohibit trucks from using streets in East Cambridge residential areas during certain hours.
Air Quality:
Regarding the establishment of an implementation program by the Authority to comply with the Boston Transportation Control Program (BTCP) and the State Motor Vehicle Emissions, Inspection and Maintenance Program (I & M), the Authority will, of course, require that developers in the Kendal Square area comply with all laws and regulations dealing with air quality, including those pertaining to the BTCP and the State Program.
Regarding the 10 percent reduction in emissions attributed to the motor vehicle emission inspection and maintenance program, our report utilized the current estimation procedure.
